import re import html # Example invitation template with placeholders. INVITATION_FORMAT = """

{event_title}

{event_description}

Date: {event_date}

{additional_notes}
""" # Whitelist of tags that are considered safe for the description and notes. ALLOWED_TAGS = {"p", "br", "strong", "em", "ul", "ol", "li", "b", "i"} def _sanitize_html(text: str) -> str: """ Escape all HTML in *text* and then re‑insert a whitelist of allowed tags. This is a very small, self‑contained sanitizer that does not depend on external libraries. It should be sufficient for simple invitation content. """ # First escape everything to neutralise any malicious markup escaped = html.escape(text) # Re‑insert allowed tags: we look for the escaped form of each tag # and replace it with the real tag. for tag in ALLOWED_TAGS: open_tag = f"<{tag}>" close_tag = f"</{tag}>" escaped = escaped.replace(open_tag, f"<{tag}>") escaped = escaped.replace(close_tag, f"") return escaped def prepare_event_details( headline: str, summary: str, scheduled_date: str, additional_info: str ) -> str: """ Generate a secure, sanitized HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title or name of the event. summary : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain paragraphs and basic formatting). scheduled_date : str The scheduled date of the event. additional_info : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the event organizer. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML suitable for safe display. """ if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (headline, summary, scheduled_date, additional_info)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be strings.") safe_title = html.escape(headline) safe_summary = _sanitize_html(summary) safe_date = html.escape(scheduled_date) safe_notes = _sanitize_html(additional_info) return INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_summary, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes )
